## Current Role

Dr. Andrew Dauber, MD, MMSc, is the Chief of the Division of Endocrinology at Children's National Hospital in Washington, DC [1][2]. He holds the academic title of Associate Professor of Pediatrics at the George Washington University School of Medicine and Health Sciences [3]. In his role as Division Chief, he leads clinical and research programs in pediatric endocrinology and diabetes at Children's National.

Previously, Dr. Dauber served as a faculty physician in the Division of Endocrinology at Boston Children's Hospital and as an instructor at Harvard Medical School [4][5].

## Medical Education and Training

**Medical School:** Dr. Dauber earned his MD and MMSc (Master of Medical Sciences) from Harvard Medical School [3][4]. The MMSc degree reflects his research training emphasis during his graduate medical education.

**Undergraduate:** Dr. Dauber completed his undergraduate education at Columbia University prior to medical school [6].

**Residency:** He completed his pediatric residency at Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School (Pediatrics, approximately 2004-2007) [4][5].

**Fellowship:** Dr. Dauber completed a clinical and research fellowship in Pediatric Endocrinology at Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School (approximately 2007-2010) [4][5]. During his fellowship he began his research focus on the genetics of growth disorders and precocious puberty.

**Research Training:** Following fellowship, Dr. Dauber remained at Boston Children's Hospital as a research fellow and then faculty, working in the laboratory of Dr. Joel Hirschhorn at the Broad Institute and Boston Children's Hospital, focusing on genomic approaches to pediatric growth disorders [4].
